newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli police to probe corruption charges.
newsitem.headline: Israeli police to probe corruption charges.

text.p: Israeli police will investigate allegations by state-owned television of corruption in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet's short-lived appointment of an attorney general, a police spokeswoman said on Friday.
"The general inspector asked the head of the investigations department to start investigating on Sunday," spokeswoman Linda Menuhin told Reuters. "So the police will start investigating on Sunday."

Earlier on Friday, Netanyahu called for a police inquiry "to reach the truth of the matter as soon as possible." His office said he made a statement calling for the probe at the start of a cabinet meeting.

The television said on Wednesday that Netanyahu had appointed lawyer Roni Bar-On as attorney general two weeks ago at the behest of Arye Deri, an ex-cabinet minister on trial for corruption charges, whose Shas party is a key coalition member.
The television said Bar-On promised Deri a plea bargain in his trial in return for Shas giving Netanyahu vital support for a deal with the PLO on redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Bar-On resigned within 12 hours of taking office under public criticism he was unfit for the job. Bar-On denied the television's allegations, as did Netanyahu and Deri.
